chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about dates and raisins — what is the minimum that makes zakat obligatory on them? He said: Five awsaq.
And the Mi'a Fa'ira and Umm Ju'rur (two inferior date varieties) are left out — zakat is not paid on them even if they are numerous.
And one or two clusters are left for the guard who is among the palm trees watching over them, and that is left for his dependents.

key_terms.أَوْسَاق: Awsaq (singular: wasq) — a classical measure of dry goods; five awsaq equals 300 sa'
key_terms.أُمُّ جُعْرُورٍ: Umm Ju'rur — another inferior date variety, also exempt from zakat
key_terms.الزَّكَاة: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.الْحَارِس: Al-haris — the watchman/guard of the orchard
key_terms.الْعَذْق: Al-'adhq — a cluster or bunch of dates from a palm tree
key_terms.مِعَى فَأْرَةٍ: Mi'a Fa'ira — an inferior or undesirable variety of date, exempt from zakat

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum nisab of dates and raisins that makes zakat obligatory in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the nisab (minimum threshold) for zakat on dates and raisins as five awsaq (a standard measure equivalent to approximately 300 sa' or around 612 kg). He further specifies two important exemptions: certain inferior-quality date varieties (Mi'a Fa'ira and Umm Ju'rur) are never subject to zakat regardless of quantity; and one or two clusters of dates are customarily set aside as compensation for the orchard guard and his family. This ruling illustrates the Shia jurisprudential tradition of balancing obligations of wealth purification with practical protections for agricultural workers.
